description: Portable GraphQL synthesis scenarios: one operation per operation definition, addressed by operation name, with the schema carried in either representation; and the two whole-source refusals the load gates make faithful. Scenarios GQL-SS-07 to -17 assert the derived input and output schemas of §6 and §7. A named operation definition's key is its name (§11.2); the key of a lone anonymous operation and the resolution of a key collision between sources are synthesis policy under §11.4, so a scenario asserting one of those pins the reference synthesizer's spelling and a synthesizer spelling it otherwise fails only the key comparison. Each names the synthesizer rules it exercises. No scenario addresses a lone anonymous operation, because its key is §11.4's declared freedom and a coverage entry must name a key; the projection-name rule for one is decided by §7's text alone.

scenarios.description: Every named operation definition of the carried document becomes one operation, addressed by its name, typed against the type-system-language schema.
The same document against the same schema carried as an introspection result synthesizes the same operations; the two schema representations are one interpreted schema.
A location-only source carries no document and denotes no operation: whole-source refusal at the content-shape gate.
A location in a scheme the incorporated transport does not define refuses at the location gate.
With content.subscriptions absent, the subscription definition is accounted invalid and yields no operation, while the query definition is represented.

content.document:
query Status { status }
subscription Ticks { ticks }
content.schema:
type Query { status: String }
type Subscription { ticks: Int }

scenarios.description: An unused fragment invalidates the whole inventory: synthesis emits no operation and accounts every definition invalid; the source is not refused.
Input schema: scalar variables derive by the table with nullability composed; required lists the non-null variables without a default; no additionalProperties keyword.

content.document: query S($i: Int!, $f: Float, $s: String!, $b: Boolean, $id: ID!) { s(i: $i, f: $f, s: $s, b: $b, id: $id) }
content.schema: type Query { s(i: Int!, f: Float, s: String!, b: Boolean, id: ID!): String }

scenarios.description: Input schema: an enum with a default carries the default's image and no type member; a OneOf input object carries minProperties, maxProperties, and non-null properties.

content.document: query E($st: Status = ACTIVE, $filter: Filter!) { e(st: $st, filter: $filter) }

scenarios.description: Input schema: a list position is an anyOf of the array and the single value, nullability applied to the item and then to the list.

content.schema: type Query { l(ids: [ID!]): String }

scenarios.description: Output schema: the whole data map with every collected response name required and additionalProperties false, nested objects likewise, leaves by the output pins.

content.document: query V($id: ID!) { viewer(id: $id) { id name } status }

scenarios.description: Output schema: a selection on an abstract type yields one branch per possible concrete type in the interpreted schema's order, __typename as a const in each, combined with anyOf before nullability.

content.document: query N($id: ID!) { node(id: $id) { id __typename ... on User { name } } }

scenarios.description: Output schema: a response name whose only contributor is variable-conditioned is present but not required.

content.document: query C($show: Boolean!, $id: ID!) { status @include(if: $show) viewer(id: $id) { id } }

scenarios.description: Custom scalars: an unconstrained schema carrying the scalar's name in format and its specification URL in x-graphql-specifiedBy, with nullability composed around it; the position is a projection entry.

content.schema:
scalar DateTime @specifiedBy(url: "https://scalars.graphql.org/andimarek/date-time")
type Query { at(when: DateTime!): DateTime }

scenarios.description: A recursive input type is cut into a referenced schema; the reference position carries nullability by anyOf and the cut-point key is synthesis policy.

content.schema:
input Node { value: Int child: Node }
type Query { r(n: Node): String }

scenarios.description: A OneOf member takes exclude null in place of admit null: an enum member, having no type member, is wrapped in allOf with not-null; a nullable list of nullable strings composes item nullability, the singleton type collapse, and list nullability.
__typename on an object type is a constant; a variable-free operation's input carries empty properties and required.

content.schema:
type Query { viewer(id: ID!): User }
type User { id: ID! }

scenarios.description: A custom-scalar field selected under a list is one projection position named by response names with list indices omitted; a custom-scalar input-object field is named by its coordinate once.
A definition under a built-in scalar name reads as that built-in scalar: an enum written as Int leaves Int an unbounded integer in the output schema.

content.schema:
enum Int { ONE }
type Query { n: Int }

scenarios.description: Deprecated fields and input fields the operation reaches are included in the derived schemas and annotated by projection entries named with the #deprecated suffix; the operation stays represented.

content.schema:
input Filter { after: String @deprecated(reason: "use since") since: String }
type Query { old(n: Filter): String @deprecated(reason: "use new") new: String }

scenarios.description: An annotative introspection member absent at a reached element (isDeprecated on User.name) makes every operation reaching it lossy, with a projection entry naming the element and the member; the operation is still emitted.

content.document: query Viewer($id: ID!) { viewer(id: $id) { id name } }

scenarios.description: Abstract-type branches whose derived schemas are identical collapse to one at the first of their positions, and a single remaining branch stands as the position's schema with no anyOf; a __typename selection keeps the branches distinct through its const.

content.document:
query A { node { id } }
query B { node { __typename id } }

scenarios.description: A variable definition's description is emitted as description on the outermost schema the position carries after nullability composition, beside default; no other derived schema carries one.

content.document: query Q("the viewer's id" $id: ID!, "since when" $w: DateTime = null) { viewer(id: $id, since: $w) { id } }

scenarios.description: A selection with a literal @include(if: false) is excluded exactly as CollectFields would exclude it at execution, and a literal @skip(if: false) leaves its selection included and required.

content.document: query Q { a @include(if: false) b @skip(if: false) }
content.schema: type Query { a: String b: String }

scenarios.description: A literal exclusion wins over a variable condition on the same selection; two selections of one response name merge their sub-selections as CollectSubfields does, and the name is required when any contributor is unconditioned; a variable condition on a fragment spread makes the spread's selections variable-conditioned.

content.schema:
type User { id: ID! name: String }
type Query { a: String viewer: User status: String }

scenarios.description: An input field's declared default is emitted as the field's JSON Schema default on the outermost schema the position carries, under the fixed image for string, list, float, boolean, and object literals, and a defaulted field is not required.

A pinned result's defaultValue on an input field is a GraphQL-language string parsed under the const-value grammar before the JSON image: a list literal becomes a JSON array and a string literal a JSON string, emitted as the field's default.

A pinned input field's defaultValue string that does not parse as a const value is read as the annotative member absent: the operation reaching the field is lossy with an entry naming the element and the member, and the field carries no default.

An argument is reached when the operation supplies it or the edition requires it, and an enum value when a literal names it or the enum types a position the operation reaches: the unsupplied nullable deprecated argument yields no entry, the literal reaches only A, and the variable-typed enum reaches every value, so B's deprecation is recorded.

content.document: query Q($k: K) { f(b: 1) g(k: A) h(k: $k) }
content.schema:
enum K { A B @deprecated(reason: "gone") }
type Query { f(a: Int @deprecated(reason: "unused"), b: Int): Int g(k: K): Int h(k: K): Int }

scenarios.description: A selection inside __schema derives its output schema from the September 2025 introspection types: __Schema.queryType is __Type! and __Type.name is String.

content.schema: type Query { status: String }

scenarios.description: An operation definition's description (September 2025 §2.2) is the operation's description, and a non-null list variable is the list-or-single anyOf with null excluded.

content.schema: type Query { things(ids: [Int!]!): [Int] }

scenarios.description: An enum output leaf is its value-name enum, with null admitted through anyOf at a nullable position and excluded through allOf at a non-null one, since an enum schema has no type member.

content.schema:
enum K { A B }
type Query { k: K kk: K! }

scenarios.description: A selection on an abstract type with no possible types derives type null at a nullable position and false at a non-null one; no schema is ever an empty anyOf.

content.document:
query E { node { id } }
query F { nn { id } }
content.schema:
interface Node { id: ID! }
type Query { node: Node nn: Node! }

scenarios.description: Projection positions are named on the emitted contract after collapse: a custom scalar under a single surviving branch carries no bracket segment, while the same scalar under two surviving branches is two positions.

content.document:
query N { node { at } }
query M { node { __typename at } }

scenarios.description: A source that refuses as a source at resolution (two definitions sharing one name and no other) is, to synthesis, a loaded source whose every definition is invalid: no operation, one entry per definition, the entries referenced by name and document ordinal.

content.document:
query A { status }
query A { status }
content.schema: type Query { status: String }

scenarios.description: A projection entry carries the status of its class whatever the owning operation's disposition: on a lossy operation the custom scalar entry is represented and the annotative-absence entry lossy.

content.document: query V($id: ID!) { viewer(id: $id) { id name at } }

scenarios.description: An anonymous operation definition that is not alone fails §5.2.3.1 for the whole inventory; its coverage entry is referenced by # and its ordinal under §7's empty-name rule.

content.schema: type Query { status: String }

scenarios.description: A deprecated argument the operation supplies is reached and recorded by its schema coordinate with the #deprecated suffix.

content.schema: type Query { f(a: Int @deprecated(reason: "x")): Int }

scenarios.description: A definition occupying no addressable position is referenced by its name and its ordinal among the document's operation definitions, wherever it occurs: B stays addressable and represented while the two A definitions are A#2 and A#3.

content.schema: type Query { status: String }

scenarios.description: A branch's leaf is typed from the concrete type's own field definition, as ExecuteField reads it: a covariantly non-null implementer yields a branch that differs from its sibling, so the branches do not collapse and each carries its own projection position.
Branch order follows the interpreted schema: a union's listed members first and an extension's members after them in document order, whatever order the member types are defined in.

An interface's Object implementers are ordered by the document position of the definition or extension that declares the implementation: User, declaring it in its definition, precedes Post, which declares it in a later extension although Post is defined first.
In an introspection result branch order is possibleTypes order, not the order of types: Post precedes User although types lists User first.
A pinned result carrying a chain deeper than nine wrappers is read as carried: the output schema nests ten list levels around the leaf.
A list position's single-value branch is the item's declared-type schema with exclude null applied, which for a schema without a type member is the allOf form even where the item is nullable.

content.schema:
enum Kind { A B }
type Query { t(k: [Kind]): Int }

scenarios.description: Types that refer to themselves through other types are all cut: both members of a mutual recursion are referenced at every occurrence.

content.document: query R($a: A, $b: B) { r(a: $a, b: $b) }

scenarios.description: Output object schemas are keyed by response name: two aliases of one field are two properties, both required, and two projection positions.

content.document: query Q { a: at b: at }
content.schema:
scalar DateTime
type Query { at: DateTime }

scenarios.description: A pinned October 2021 result lacks isOneOf and specifiedByURL on every element; both are edition exceptions read as false and null, with no lossy disposition: the input object carries no OneOf constraint, and no annotative-absence entry is recorded.
A non-null variable with a default is not required; Int and enum defaults on variables take the fixed image; an extended input type's properties follow definition then extension order.

content.document: query V($x: Int! = 5, $k: Kind = A, $f: F) { v(x: $x, k: $k, f: $f) }

scenarios.description: A deprecated enum value is reached through an output enum the operation selects and recorded by its coordinate.

content.schema:
enum K { A B @deprecated(reason: "gone") }
type Query { k: K }

scenarios.description: A selection a literal condition does not exclude is variable-conditioned when it also carries a variable condition: the response name is present and not required.

content.schema: type Query { a: String }
